# KodeCite.ai — Full Reference

> KodeCite builds owned business infrastructure for the agent-driven web. We make a business understandable, verifiable, recommendable, actionable, and controlled — so people, search engines, and AI agents can use the same authoritative record.

KodeCite.ai is based in North Idaho and builds for service businesses anywhere. The website, Next.js, schema, entity graph, llms.txt, agent.json, APIs, forms, and future MCP are components. The product is an accurate business model plus controlled machine use.

This file is identity and discovery. KodeCite does not currently publish an autonomous agent submission endpoint on kodecite.ai. This llms-full.txt is the expanded companion to /llms.txt.

## The principle

AI should not merely find a business. It should understand what the business does, know what it is allowed to do, and take the next safe step with a customer.

## The problem

Most businesses are spread across a website, directories, forms, calendars, and unwritten rules. AI may find pieces. It cannot reliably reconstruct what the business can do or safely act. That is an infrastructure problem, not a content-volume problem.

WordPress, Wix, and Squarespace are common platforms. They are not blank to every AI crawler. They often make it harder to publish one owned, consistent, machine-usable record. A full Next.js rebuild is the strongest path. A KodeCite-owned sidecar may fit selected pilots.

## The five-layer model

### 01 — Truth
Identity, people, services, products, locations and service areas, credentials, proof, policies, and limitations — published as one authoritative record.

### 02 — Capability
What can be requested, what information is required, where the business works, which services are available, and what success does — and does not — mean.

### 03 — Control
Human confirmation, authorization, validation, rate limiting, idempotency, and fail-closed behavior. No false booking, pricing, purchase, or acceptance.

### 04 — Action
Submit a consultation, send a qualified inquiry, request an appointment, or hand off to a human. Schedule or transact later only where the real business permits it. Not every client needs every action.

### 05 — Distribution
Website, search, structured data and entity graphs, external profiles, llms.txt, agent.json, capability discovery, protected APIs, and future MCP or browser agents. These are delivery surfaces — not the product category.

Not every AI system reads llms.txt, agent.json, or schema. Those files help when a system looks for them. They do not make AI know a business with certainty.

## What you get

### Foundation Build — $4,995
Owned website (Next.js where appropriate), canonical truth, entity graph, services and geography, corroboration, machine discovery, and a capability map. Client-owned GitHub and Vercel. Does not automatically include a production action endpoint.

### Agent Capability Build
Custom-scoped after business rules are understood. One defined action at a time: contract, validation, security and abuse controls, idempotency, human handoff, production acceptance testing. No published price. Different actions carry different rules and risk.

### Platform Capability Layer — Pilot
For selected WordPress / Wix / Squarespace businesses remaining on those platforms: a KodeCite-owned Next.js/Vercel sidecar on a business-controlled domain or subdomain. No WordPress plugin dependency. Truth and capability publication, plus protected actions where appropriate. Application-only. Not universally proven.

### Agent Readiness Review
See what AI can understand, verify, and safely do with a business today. Free written review in 24–48 hours when operationally available. Request at https://www.kodecite.ai/machine-read

## Acceptance standard

Before a build, we agree what the system must publish, what AI must be able to understand, and — when an action is included — what the protected workflow must successfully do. The engagement is not complete until those agreed outputs pass tests. This is not a citation money-back guarantee and not a promise that a specific AI engine will cite the business.

## Who it is for

Established high-trust, high-value service businesses. KodeCite is not a chatbot agency, a generic AI-automation shop, an SEO retainer, or a paid-media practice. We do not publish MCP or an action endpoint without reconciling the real business.

## Production proof — Luxe Window Works

Luxe publishes a machine-readable in-home consultation capability:

https://www.luxewindowworks.com/api/capabilities/request-in-home-consultation

Contract 1.0. Readiness: request-submission-ready. Submission enabled. Human follow-up required. Booking, pricing, and checkout unavailable.

Authorized production test: one valid request returned HTTP 200 accepted / in_service_area and the email reached the Luxe inbox. The identical duplicate returned the original outcome and did not send a second email. The same key with a changed payload returned HTTP 409 idempotency_conflict. No appointment, price, purchase, or project acceptance was claimed.

Significance: an outside agent could discover what Luxe permits, determine qualification, submit safely, and receive an honest machine-readable outcome.

Discovery screenshots (ChatGPT, Google, Bing, Gemini) are separate evidence that visibility can follow better infrastructure. They are not the product category.

Full case study: https://www.kodecite.ai/blog/from-recommended-to-actionable-luxe-window-works

## Ownership

The client owns the repo, the site, and the deployed infrastructure. No mandatory retainer. Active capabilities may use third-party services with direct costs. APIs, credentials, and security may need maintenance. KodeCite does not claim an active endpoint runs forever without that work.
